Hi all — looping in some concrete answers and a recommended config. Jonas and I also attached a short config snippet and the PSC/DNS note to the Drive link.

Answers to Samir's questions:
1) PSC/DNS: Private Service Connect will publish an internal DNS target that you can map in your VPC. We recommend creating a private DNS zone pointing the service name to the PSC endpoint IP. PSC will NAT inbound traffic to Redwood's Private control plane. No public route required.

2) mTLS scope: Our recommended pattern is:
   - Control plane (management/authentication): mTLS + token-based mutual auth (recommended) — Redwood will validate client certs issued by your PKI.
   - Data plane (inference calls): token-based auth (short-lived JWTs) for most workloads to avoid per-request mTLS handshake overhead; if you have strict regulatory requirements we can enable mTLS on the inference path (expect higher latency and additional connection management).

3) Webhook callbacks: We can deliver callbacks over private egress if you expose an internal endpoint reachable from our egress CIDR or via PSC peering. If you prefer not to open any inbound routes, we can instead push callback data to a mutually accessible storage (GCS) and signal via a control-plane webhook that contains a signed fetch URL.

Attached: redwood-vpc-psc-dns-notes.md (Drive link), finpay-vpc-architecture-draft.pdf (updated with PSC notes)

Next steps:
- Samir/Priya: confirm CIDR ranges and whether you want inference mTLS enabled for the POC.
- We'll update the quickstart with the PSC DNS snippet and a short example for issuing client certs and configuring token exchange.

Happy to jump on the network call next week — propose Tue Jun 16 10:00 AM PT if that works for you.

Best,
